course.name: Maths Foundations for Machine Learning (demo chain)
course.note: Hand-curated demo chain for the Punca prototype. Every edge was written and reviewed by a person. Replace or extend with real APU module content (with permission).

concepts.name: Fractions and ratios
concepts.description: Simplifying, adding, multiplying and dividing fractions, and expressing one quantity as a ratio of another.

concepts.name: Exponents and powers
concepts.description: Rules for powers: multiplying powers adds exponents, a power of a power multiplies them, negative and zero exponents, and the number e.

concepts.name: Rearranging equations
concepts.description: Solving equations, making a variable the subject, substituting values and expanding brackets.

concepts.name: Logarithms
concepts.description: The logarithm as the inverse of exponentiation, the log rules, and the natural log ln.

concepts.name: Functions
concepts.description: A function maps each input to exactly one output; f(x) notation, domain, range and graphs.

concepts.name: Function composition
concepts.description: Feeding one function into another, f(g(x)): identifying the inner and outer function and the order they are applied.

concepts.name: Linear functions and slope
concepts.description: Straight lines y = mx + c: slope as rise over run, and the y-intercept.

concepts.name: Summation notation
concepts.description: Sigma notation for adding up a sequence of terms, with an index that runs over a range.

concepts.name: Limits
concepts.description: The value a function approaches as its input approaches a point or infinity; the idea the derivative is built on.

concepts.name: Derivatives
concepts.description: The derivative as the instantaneous rate of change: the slope of the tangent line at a point.

concepts.name: Basic differentiation rules
concepts.description: The power rule, constant multiple rule and sum rule for differentiating polynomials and simple powers.

concepts.name: Chain rule
concepts.description: Differentiating a composite function: the derivative of f(g(x)) is f'(g(x)) times g'(x).

concepts.name: Derivatives of exp and log
concepts.description: The derivative of e^x is e^x and the derivative of ln x is 1/x.

concepts.name: Partial derivatives
concepts.description: Differentiating a function of several variables with respect to one of them while holding the others constant.

concepts.name: Vectors
concepts.description: Ordered lists of numbers: adding vectors, multiplying by a scalar, and the length (magnitude) of a vector.

concepts.name: Dot product
concepts.description: Multiplying two vectors element by element and summing the results; zero means the vectors are perpendicular.

concepts.name: Gradient
concepts.description: The vector of all partial derivatives of a function; it points in the direction of steepest increase.

concepts.name: Matrices and shapes
concepts.description: Rectangular arrays of numbers described by rows by columns, and how to index their entries.

concepts.name: Matrix multiplication
concepts.description: Multiplying an m×n matrix by an n×p matrix gives m×p; each entry is the dot product of a row and a column.

concepts.name: Matrix transpose
concepts.description: Swapping the rows and columns of a matrix, so an m×n matrix becomes n×m.

concepts.name: Basic probability
concepts.description: Events and outcomes, probabilities between 0 and 1, complements, and multiplying probabilities of independent events.

concepts.name: Conditional probability
concepts.description: The probability of A given that B happened: P(A|B) = P(A and B) / P(B).

concepts.name: Bayes' theorem
concepts.description: Updating a prior belief with evidence: P(A|B) = P(B|A) P(A) / P(B).

concepts.name: Random variables and expected value
concepts.description: A random variable assigns numbers to outcomes; its expected value is the probability-weighted average E[X] = Σ x P(x).

concepts.name: Mean, variance and standard deviation
concepts.description: The average of a set of values, and the variance and standard deviation that measure how spread out they are.

concepts.name: Loss functions
concepts.description: A loss function measures how wrong a model's predictions are; mean squared error is the standard example.

concepts.name: Gradient descent
concepts.description: Training by repeatedly stepping the weights against the gradient of the loss: w ← w − η∇L, with learning rate η.

concepts.name: Linear regression
concepts.description: Fitting a line (or hyperplane) y = wx + b to data by minimising the mean squared error.

concepts.name: Sigmoid function
concepts.description: σ(z) = 1 / (1 + e^(−z)) squashes any real number into the range 0 to 1.

concepts.name: Cross-entropy loss
concepts.description: The log loss for classifiers: −[y ln p + (1 − y) ln(1 − p)], which punishes confident wrong predictions heavily.

concepts.name: Logistic regression
concepts.description: Binary classification by passing a linear score through the sigmoid to get P(y = 1), trained with cross-entropy.

concepts.name: Softmax
concepts.description: Turns a vector of scores (logits) into probabilities that are positive and sum to 1.

concepts.name: Activation functions
concepts.description: Non-linear functions such as ReLU, sigmoid and tanh applied after each layer's weighted sum.

concepts.name: Artificial neuron
concepts.description: A neuron computes a weighted sum of its inputs plus a bias, z = w·x + b, then applies an activation.

concepts.name: Neural network forward pass
concepts.description: Computing a network's output layer by layer: each layer applies a = f(Wx + b).

concepts.name: Backpropagation
concepts.description: Computing the gradient of the loss for every weight by applying the chain rule backwards through the network.

concepts.name: Overfitting and validation
concepts.description: When a model fits the training data too closely and generalises badly; detected with validation and test sets.
